clue.text: Money may be obtained from many a debtor

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
a debtor is someone who owes, an ower

explanation.surface: A lender hopes to recover cash from his many borrowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' is the old crossword trick for a large Roman numeral, here D (500).
explanation.definitionFit: A dower is the portion of an estate left to a widow, a sum of wealth.

clue.text: Daughter is put on edge over a good man's lying

parts.note: taken as written
to hone a blade is to put an edge on it
ST stands for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A girl sharpens a knife over a decent man's falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on edge' looks like making nervous, but it means sharpen. ST (saint) is a crossword convention for a good man.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest means untruthful or deceitful.

clue.text: Don't claim a view isn't right

indicators.note: isn't right says the letters are wrong as they stand and must be put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone declines to press their case because an opinion is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive is to give up a right or forgo an entitlement.

clue.text: Practised play

parts.note: a drama that has been gone through beforehand by its cast, ready for the stage

explanation.definitionFit: Rehearsed means practised in advance, as actors do with a script.

clue.text: Sort of plants made up in bales perhaps

indicators.note: made up suggests the following letters are assembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some kind of vegetation comes baled up, perhaps like hay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' looks like one phrase, but 'made' is the anagram signal and 'up' joins IN BALES as fodder to give SUBALPINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Subalpine plants grow on mountain slopes just below the tree line, a category of flora.

clue.text: Boy about to charge for cheese

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word wraps another

parts.note: a son is a boy
to tilt is to charge with a lance, as in jousting

explanation.surface: A lad is about to rush at some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to charge' recalls jousting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a blue-veined English cheese.

clue.text: Flower as a result of insecticide use?

definitions.text: Flower as a result of insecticide use?

parts.words: Flower as a result of insecticide use?
parts.note: an insecticide kills insects, so what follows is a loss of creepy-crawlies, read as the name of a plant

explanation.surface: A bloom appears after spraying for pests.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the plant's name into two words and it describes what spraying insecticide achieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugloss is a bristly blue-flowered plant of the borage family.

clue.text: The old doctor's a sucker!

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a physician

explanation.definitionFit: Leech was once a word for a physician, and it is also a bloodsucking worm used in medicine.

clue.text: Popular instrument — a single note shows nothing can touch it

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a viola is a stringed instrument
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fashionable fiddle playing one note proves untouchable.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means unharmed and safe from violation.

clue.text: A resort of high-fliers

parts.note: a resort suggests a holiday place for jet-setters, but the high-fliers are birds of prey

explanation.surface: A holiday spot for the jet set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-fliers' suggests the wealthy; it means eagles.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built high on a cliff.

clue.text: Scorning to produce notes about fire

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word wraps another

parts.note: to produce musical notes is to sing
to fire a lamp or fuse is to light it

explanation.surface: Someone sneers while writing music about a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Slighting someone is treating them with disdain or contempt.

clue.text: Young swimmer constantly seen around small lake

indicators.note: seen around says one word is placed so it encircles another

parts.note: constantly means for ever, at all times
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A youngster always swims round a little pond.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a fish that swims upriver.

clue.text: Nothing settled by a musical performance

parts.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Nothing was decided by a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set entirely to music, sung by performers.

clue.text: Being very nice over the MO'S error

parts.note: too means very, as in not too bad

indicators.note: error suggests the letters of these words are set down wrongly, in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A doctor is being too kind, which is a medical officer's mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor; 'error' muddles THE MO'S. 'nice' is used in its sense of tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome food is pleasant to eat, delicious and appealing.

clue.text: Writer taking issue after soldiers' rebuff

indicators.note: after places the offspring behind the soldiers' letters
a rebuff pushes something back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a son is issue, meaning offspring

explanation.surface: An author takes up a complaint after troops turn him away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuff' turns the corps name round; 'issue' looks like a quarrel but means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist and poet.

clue.text: Greek dramatist in translation is perused with both eyes, you might say

indicators.note: in translation means the letters are rendered in a different arrangement

parts.note: two eyes said out loud sound like two letter Is

explanation.surface: A Greek playwright's work is read in English by someone peering hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; PERUSED plus II, the eyes heard as letters, is rearranged by 'in translation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the three great tragedians of ancient Athens.

clue.text: They are no singers of low songs!

definitions.text: They are no singers of low songs!

parts.words: They are no singers of low songs!
parts.note: low songs might be vulgar ditties, but the clue means singers whose voices are high, not low

explanation.surface: Some performers refuse to sing coarse ballads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like vulgar; it means low in pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani, the Italian plural of soprano, are the highest female voices.

clue.text: One who'll pay for catty utterance about Charles English!

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word wraps the others

parts.note: a cat's contented sound is a purr

explanation.surface: A buyer purrs about an Englishman named Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchaser is a buyer, someone paying for goods.

clue.text: Rent etc, is possibly making one cross

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Bills such as rent may annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but here it is a verb, to meet across.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to pass across or through each other.

clue.text: One involved in deals will get streams of abuse

indicators.note: involved in means placed within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: deals are trades, business transactions
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A party to business deals will get shouted at.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches, outbursts of criticism.

clue.text: An immigrant arranging 27?

definitions.meaning: a newcomer who makes a home in a new land
27 is discharge: one who settles a debt

explanation.definitionFit: A settler colonises new territory, and one who settles an account discharges it.

clue.text: Turned scarlet and left the river

indicators.note: turned means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: scarlet is a bright red
left means departed, went

explanation.surface: Someone blushed and walked away from the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned scarlet' looks like blushing, but 'Turned' reverses RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derwent is the name of several English rivers, in Cumbria, Derbyshire and Yorkshire.

clue.text: Get mad with some trader, angered beyond tolerance

indicators.note: some means only part of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Become furious with a shopkeeper who is beyond patience.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange someone is to drive them insane.

clue.text: Drink with stout defender

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer like stout

explanation.surface: A fan having a pint of stout.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter backs or upholds a person or cause.

clue.text: Repaired for only five hundred!

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Fixed up for just five hundred!
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler repairs shoes by giving them new soles.
explanation.definitionFit: Soled shoes have been given new bottoms, mended by a cobbler.

clue.text: Black magic

parts.note: sorcery practised in the Caribbean

explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of sorcery or witchcraft practised in the West Indies.

clue.text: He really doesn't like causing heart-break

indicators.note: break means the word heart is smashed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes others goes about breaking hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: A hater is someone who detests, the opposite of a fan.

clue.text: Object when spare key is demanded

parts.note: spare means lean, thin
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone protests when asked for a duplicate key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any item or article.

clue.text: The home of a man of science

definitions.meaning: a gatekeeper's cottage or a small house on an estate
Sir Oliver ..., British physicist and radio pioneer

explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small dwelling, and Oliver Lodge was a physicist who worked on wireless telegraphy.

clue.text: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip

definitions.text: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip

parts.words: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip
parts.note: grounding sounds like education and slip like an error, but it is earth that gave way under a hillside

explanation.surface: Poor schooling caused a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounding' and 'slip' pretend to be about learning and error; read literally, unstable ground slides away.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is a mass of earth and rock collapsing down a slope.

clue.text: Cashier is to tax first head of department

indicators.note: first says this letter goes at the front of the rest
head of means take the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written
to tax someone is to charge them

explanation.surface: A bank teller must bill the department boss first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a bank clerk, but it is a verb: to dismiss from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them from the armed forces.

clue.text: Honourable Conservative?

explanation.definitionFit: Right means just and fitting, and the Right is the conservative wing of politics.
